questions.text: Which sequence describes the lesson’s three levels of progressive disclosure?

options.A: Load every reference, then select a skill, then read its description.
options.B: Publish compact catalog metadata, load the selected body, then load needed supporting resources.
options.C: Execute scripts, grant tool permissions, then validate the package.
options.D: Activate all installed skills, merge their bodies, then trim unrelated results.

questions.explanation: Catalog metadata supports selection, the active body provides the procedure, and branch-specific resources are loaded only when needed.

questions.text: A skill covers Python packages, containers, and documentation releases. How should its entry body guide resource loading?

options.A: Require every guide at activation so no constraint can be missed.
options.B: Say read the relevant guide without naming files or conditions.
options.C: Hide the central workflow in a deep chain of unnamed references.
options.D: Give direct file paths and load conditions for each artifact type.

questions.explanation: Direct branch-specific references make resource reachability and loading decisions observable while avoiding irrelevant context.

questions.text: validate_reference rejects every symlink in the path before resolving the final target. references/guide.md is a symlink to another file inside the same skill. What happens?

options.A: It raises ReferencePathError because this implementation forbids symlinks even within the package.
options.B: It accepts the link because the final target stays inside the package.
options.C: It reads the link text as the reference content without following it.
options.D: It accepts the link only when its target is at most 12,000 characters.

questions.explanation: The explicit is_symlink check raises before final target containment. This lab’s policy is stricter than allowing contained symlinks.
